1	# Renewable Energy Cost Revolution: LCOE, Capacity & Fossil Fuel Subsidies (2010–2024)
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This collection of four datasets tracks the economic transformation of the global energy sector from 2010 to 2024. It covers the declining levelized cost of energy for solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage; the cost range of new fossil fuel generation; cumulative renewable installed capacity; and annual global fossil fuel subsidies.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### lcoe_trends
     9	Annual LCOE values for three technologies: `solar_pv`, `onshore_wind`, and `battery_storage`. All values in 2023 real USD per MWh. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV ranges from 359 to 33; onshore wind from 95 to 35; battery storage from 1,100 to 102.
    10	
    11	### fossil_fuel_lcoe_range
    12	Biennial LCOE ranges for new-build gas CCGT (`gas_ccgt_low`, `gas_ccgt_high`) and coal (`coal_low`, `coal_high`). 8 rows at even-year intervals. Values in 2023 real USD/MWh. These define the reference band against which renewable crossover points are identified.
    13	
    14	### installed_capacity
    15	Cumulative global installed capacity in GW for `solar_pv_gw` and `onshore_wind_gw`. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV grows from 40 to 1,950 GW; onshore wind from 178 to 960 GW.
    16	
    17	### fossil_fuel_subsidies
    18	Annual global fossil fuel subsidies in nominal billion USD, split into `consumption_subsidies_bn` and `production_subsidies_bn`, with a `total_subsidies_bn` sum. 15 rows (2010–2024). Total ranges from ~290 to ~700 billion.
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- LCOE figures are illustrative estimates aligned with IRENA and BloombergNEF reporting trends but rounded for clarity.
    22	- Battery storage LCOE reflects 4-hour lithium-ion systems.
    23	- 2022 spike in fossil LCOE and subsidies reflects the global energy price crisis.
    24	- Fossil fuel subsidy estimates cover direct government subsidies only; implicit subsidies (e.g., unpriced externalities) are excluded.
    25	- 2024 values are preliminary estimates.

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Extract datasets
lcoe = data['lcoe_trends']['data']
fossil = data['fossil_fuel_lcoe_range']['data']
capacity = data['installed_capacity']['data']
subsidies = data['fossil_fuel_subsidies']['data']

# Convert to arrays
years_lcoe = np.array([d['year'] for d in lcoe])
solar_pv = np.array([d['solar_pv'] for d in lcoe])
onshore_wind = np.array([d['onshore_wind'] for d in lcoe])
battery = np.array([d['battery_storage'] for d in lcoe])

years_cap = np.array([d['year'] for d in capacity])
solar_cap = np.array([d['solar_pv_gw'] for d in capacity])
wind_cap = np.array([d['onshore_wind_gw'] for d in capacity])

years_sub = np.array([d['year'] for d in subsidies])
sub_total = np.array([d['total_subsidies_bn'] for d in subsidies])

years_fossil = np.array([d['year'] for d in fossil])
gas_low = np.array([d['gas_ccgt_low'] for d in fossil])
gas_high = np.array([d['gas_ccgt_high'] for d in fossil])
coal_low = np.array([d['coal_low'] for d in fossil])
coal_high = np.array([d['coal_high'] for d in fossil])

# Interpolate fossil ranges to all years for smooth fill
all_years = np.arange(2010, 2025)

from scipy.interpolate import interp1d
# We'll use linear interpolation for fossil ranges
f_gas_low = interp1d(years_fossil, gas_low, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')
f_gas_high = interp1d(years_fossil, gas_high, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')
f_coal_low = interp1d(years_fossil, coal_low, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')
f_coal_high = interp1d(years_fossil, coal_high, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')

gas_low_i = f_gas_low(all_years)
gas_high_i = f_gas_high(all_years)
coal_low_i = f_coal_low(all_years)
coal_high_i = f_coal_high(all_years)

# Setup figure with dual y-axes and a secondary x-axis feel via twin axes
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'DejaVu Sans'
plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 10
plt.rcParams['axes.linewidth'] = 0.8

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create main axes
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(111)
ax1.set_xlim(2009.5, 2024.5)
ax1.set_xticks(all_years)
ax1.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in all_years], rotation=45, ha='right')

# Left y-axis: LCOE (USD/MWh)
ax1.set_ylabel('LCOE (USD / MWh, 2023 real dollars)', color='#1a1a1a', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylim(0, 1200)
ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#1a1a1a')

# Right y-axis: Installed Capacity (GW)
ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.set_ylabel('Cumulative Installed Capacity (GW)', color='#1a1a1a', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylim(0, 2200)
ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#1a1a1a')

# Third y-axis: Fossil Fuel Subsidies (Billion USD) - placed on the right, offset
ax3 = ax1.twinx()
ax3.spines['right'].set_position(('outward', 70))
ax3.set_ylabel('Annual Fossil Fuel Subsidies (Billion USD, nominal)', color='#1a1a1a', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylim(0, 800)
ax3.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#1a1a1a')

# Colors - professional editorial palette
c_solar = '#E69F00'      # amber
c_wind = '#56B4E9'       # sky blue
c_battery = '#009E73'    # teal green
c_gas = '#999999'        # grey
c_coal = '#555555'       # dark grey
c_solar_cap = '#CC79A7'  # muted pink
c_wind_cap = '#0072B2'   # deep blue
c_subsidy = '#D55E00'    # vermillion

# Plot fossil fuel LCOE ranges as filled areas (behind everything)
ax1.fill_between(all_years, gas_low_i, gas_high_i, color=c_gas, alpha=0.25, label='Gas CCGT LCOE range')
ax1.fill_between(all_years, coal_low_i, coal_high_i, color=c_coal, alpha=0.15, label='Coal LCOE range')

# Plot LCOE lines
l1, = ax1.plot(years_lcoe, solar_pv, color=c_solar, linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Solar PV LCOE')
l2, = ax1.plot(years_lcoe, onshore_wind, color=c_wind, linewidth=2.5, marker='s', markersize=5, label='Onshore Wind LCOE')
l3, = ax1.plot(years_lcoe, battery, color=c_battery, linewidth=2.5, marker='^', markersize=5, label='Battery Storage LCOE')

# Plot capacity bars
bar_width = 0.35
offset = bar_width / 2
bars1 = ax2.bar(years_cap - offset, solar_cap, bar_width, color=c_solar_cap, alpha=0.7, label='Solar PV Capacity')
bars2 = ax2.bar(years_cap + offset, wind_cap, bar_width, color=c_wind_cap, alpha=0.7, label='Onshore Wind Capacity')

# Plot subsidies as line on ax3
l4, = ax3.plot(years_sub, sub_total, color=c_subsidy, linewidth=2.5, linestyle='--', marker='D', markersize=5, label='Fossil Fuel Subsidies')

# Crossover annotations
# Solar PV crossed below gas range around 2019 (gas high ~74, solar 50)
# Onshore wind was already below gas in 2010
# Let's find when solar_pv < gas_high and onshore_wind < gas_high
solar_cross = None
for y, sp, gh in zip(years_lcoe, solar_pv, f_gas_high(years_lcoe)):
    if sp < gh:
        solar_cross = int(y)
        break

wind_cross = None
for y, wp, gh in zip(years_lcoe, onshore_wind, f_gas_high(years_lcoe)):
    if wp < gh:
        wind_cross = int(y)
        break

# Annotate solar crossover
if solar_cross:
    ax1.annotate(f'Solar PV crosses below\nnew gas range ({solar_cross})',
                xy=(solar_cross, solar_pv[years_lcoe == solar_cross][0]),
                xytext=(solar_cross - 2.5, 180),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=c_solar, lw=1.5),
                fontsize=9, color=c_solar, fontweight='bold',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', edgecolor=c_solar, alpha=0.9))

# Annotate battery cost collapse
ax1.annotate('Battery cost collapse\n$1,100 → $102 /MWh\n(−91%)',
            xy=(2024, battery[-1]),
            xytext=(2021.5, 650),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=c_battery, lw=1.5),
            fontsize=9, color=c_battery, fontweight='bold',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', edgecolor=c_battery, alpha=0.9))

# Annotate capacity acceleration
ax2.annotate('Solar PV capacity\nacceleration post-2018',
            xy=(2022, solar_cap[years_cap == 2022][0]),
            xytext=(2016.5, 1600),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=c_solar_cap, lw=1.5),
            fontsize=9, color=c_solar_cap, fontweight='bold',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', edgecolor=c_solar_cap, alpha=0.9))

# Title
fig.suptitle('The Renewable Energy Cost Revolution (2010–2024)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)
ax1.set_title('Declining LCOE and rising installed capacity contrasted against persistent fossil fuel subsidies', 
              fontsize=11, style='italic', color='#444444', pad=10)

# Combine legends
lines1, labels1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
lines2, labels2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
lines3, labels3 = ax3.get_legend_handles_labels()

# Create custom legend entries for fossil ranges
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [
    Patch(facecolor=c_gas, alpha=0.4, edgecolor=c_gas, label='Gas CCGT LCOE range'),
